s: hatch (opening in the ceiling/floor of a room, in the deck of a ship, etc.)
The hatch to the attic is jammed.
Der Kapitän öffnete die Luke und sah nach draußen.

Luke.et:
Borrowed from Low German, from Middle Low German lûke, from Old Saxon *lūka, from Proto-West Germanic *lūkā.
Cognate with Dutch luik (“hatch”) and, more distantly, doublet of Loch (“hole”) and Lücke (“gap”); see the former for more.

s: a male given name; variant form Lucas
Lukas.et: Borrowed from Latin Lūcās and Ancient Greek Λουκᾶς (Loukâs).

s: lucrative (profitable, allowing the earning of a lot of money)
